absent: Full definitions of balancing context, domain, group, runqueue, task and extended scheduler objects beyond fields observed here.
Behavior of active balancing stop routines, cookie search, clock refresh, rescheduling signals and virtual time helpers beyond their call sites.
Valid ranges and defaults for migration cost threshold, busy multiplier, maximum interval, feature toggles and statistics enablement.
Selection conditions for alternate builds covering tickless balancing, idle notification, capability checks and force idle accounting.
Synchronization and lifetime of scheduler hierarchy links, idle mask storage and compartment translation table.
Implementation of CPU set operations, per CPU accessors, single load and store helpers, atomic updates and warning helpers owned elsewhere.
Handler logic for queued core balance work and force idle occupation reporting beyond queuing and timestamp capture.

findings.text: group_balance_cpu is a globally visible helper that reports the designated balancer of a group as the first member of that group's shared balance set.
task_vruntime_update is a globally visible updater that propagates force idle sequencing into fair scheduling entities only and ignores other classes.
pick_task_idle is the idle class selection entry that returns the runqueue idle thread and emits an extended scheduler continuation notice only when already idle.
pick_next_task provides core aware next thread selection with delegation to the regular picker when core scheduling is disabled or the CPU is offline.
__scx_update_idle is a globally visible extended scheduler idle state updater that refreshes builtin masks before optionally notifying interested schedulers.
Preorder traversal helpers expose iteration over the extended scheduler hierarchy starting at the root and descending to children before siblings.
SCX_CALL_OP is a macro wrapper that forwards an operation invocation to the internal dispatcher with the operation table and the locked runqueue.
alb_stop_fn selects the link cache aware stop routine when the balancing context indicates link cache task movement and otherwise selects the generic active balancing stop routine.
should_we_balance refuses balancing when the destination lies outside the allowed set and for newly idle contexts requires an empty destination with no pending wakeup.
Periodic balancing chooses the executing CPU only when it is the earliest eligible idle member, preferring a fully idle core over an idle thread in a busy core with fallback to group order.

Imbalance statistics are untouched when statistics collection is disabled and otherwise accumulate the current imbalance into the counter matching the movement kind, with link cache task movement recording nothing.
Domain balance spacing grows with busyness, converts from milliseconds to timer units, steps back by one tick when busy to avoid harmonic alignment, and stays within a fixed floor and global ceiling.
Next balance tracking only moves the shared deadline earlier toward the domain last balance plus its current spacing.

Newly idle accounting increments attempt and success tallies and after a fixed number of attempts derives a capped efficiency ratio from elapsed scheduler time plus successes before halving both tallies.
Newly idle cost tracking retains the largest observed cost with its timestamp and otherwise decays the retained maximum by about one percent per second, reporting whether decay occurred.

Tickless idle balancing exists in two build forms where the active form requests an idle balancing kick only when idle duration exceeds migration cost and blocked load is pending, whereas the alternate form is empty.
Runqueue class tracking only lowers the recorded next class toward higher priority and provides a predicate testing whether a given class sits above the recorded value.
Extended scheduler idle handling always refreshes builtin idle sets first and only afterwards delivers explicit or owed renotification, clearing owed markers at delivery time.
Builtin idle tracking marks a CPU idle individually but marks its hardware thread group idle only once every sibling is idle, clearing the whole group when any sibling becomes busy.
Idle set selection uses a single global set when per node tracking is disabled and otherwise uses the set belonging to the CPU node.

Idle notification without nested schedulers addresses only the root when explicitly requested or owed, whereas the nested case walks descendants skipping subtrees lacking base capability and honoring bypass state.
CPU argument mapping returns the identity value by default and a table translated compartment identifier when that identifier mode is active.
Capability gap reporting is zero when nesting is absent, for the root level, or in the minimal build, and otherwise reports requested bits missing from the per CPU effective set.
Core cookie comparison treats the per runqueue idle thread as compatible with any cookie and otherwise requires equality of stored cookie values.
Core wide selection reuses a pending choice without new work when task and pick generations match and differ from the scheduled generation, otherwise it performs a fresh coordinated pick.
Core force idle state is accounted and then cleared before each fresh selection, with occupancy and timing recorded only when forced idling remains.
Core balancing is queued only for forced idle situations where core scheduling is active, a core cookie is present, and the local runqueue still holds runnable work.
Balance callback queuing ignores requests for an already linked item and any request during active push balancing, otherwise it prepends the new item.
Virtual runtime baseline propagation walks enclosing fair runqueues recording the current baseline and halts early when a level already carries the current force idle generation.
Force idle accounting exists in two build forms where the active form records only when statistics collection is enabled and the alternate form does nothing.
Scheduler random helper returns a value drawn from the calling CPU private random state.
Extended idle wrappers either delegate to the core updater when the extension is enabled or compile to an empty operation in minimal builds.
Extended idle state refresh and idle notification require the target runqueue lock to be held by the caller.
Hierarchy preorder iteration requires holding the enable mutex, the scheduler lock, or read side protection against reclamation.
Core aware next thread selection and balance callback queuing both require the involved runqueue lock to be held on entry.
Balancing context carries destination CPU with its runqueue, allowed set and domain, idleness kind, plus migration kind and current imbalance amount.

Domain state relevant here includes group list, behavior flags, base interval with busy multiplier, last balance time, per kind imbalance counters, and newly idle attempt success ratio timing plus maximum cost decay state.

Runqueue state relevant here includes CPU number, runnable count, pending wakeup flag, idle and current threads, next class marker, core pointer with pick and cookie generations, and balance callback chain with extended scheduler flags.
Scheduling group exposes a shared capacity object holding the CPU set used both for membership iteration and for deriving the designated balancer.
Extended scheduler node exposes level, child list, sibling link, per CPU effective capabilities with renotify marker, and operation presence used during idle dispatch.
Newly idle efficiency cycles through accumulation of attempts and successes, threshold triggered ratio computation with stamp refresh, and halving of tallies to age history.
Core selection generations advance task generation on every fresh pick, copy it to pick generation after coordination, and advance scheduled generation when the choice is installed or reused.
Renotification markers are armed elsewhere, observed on idle continuation picks, and cleared exactly when the owed notification is delivered to the relevant scheduler scope.
Preorder walk starts at the root on empty input, descends to the first child where present, and otherwise climbs to the nearest ancestor offering a next sibling, ending with empty.
pick_next_task serves as the scheduling entry that installs the next runnable thread for the local CPU and reschedules siblings when core coordination changes their choice.
pick_task_idle serves as the idle class entry returning the dedicated idle thread for otherwise empty selection.
nohz_newidle_balance serves as the tickless idle entry that may request deferred blocked load handling before the CPU sleeps.
Balancing environment may be observed mid hotplug with destination outside the allowed set, requiring an early refusal rather than proceeding with stale membership.
Hardware thread group idle marking is intentionally racy and suitable only as a self correcting optimization, never as a correctness gate.
Sibling task lookup may drop the runqueue lock and invalidate clocks, forcing the whole core wide selection to restart after refreshing time.

Sibling overlap between incompatible user states is avoided by ensuring an inter processor signal after the old thread is no longer running, with a one time check that final choices remain compatible.
Offline siblings may have no coordinated choice prepared and must be skipped silently since they will self select when they return.
Newly idle efficiency uses a trigger threshold of 1024 attempts, a ratio ceiling of 1024, and a time to ratio shift of 22 bits when rate scaling is enabled.
Maximum newly idle cost decays by factor 253 over 256 after one second has elapsed since the previous decay timestamp.
Balance interval is clamped to a minimum of 1 timer unit and idle thread search uses minus 1 as the empty marker for no candidate yet.
